transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um, yeah, so I'm here because I'm having a lot of trouble at work. I work at a meat processing plant—which isn't really what I planned to do after getting my bachelor's degree, but you know how the job market is right now. Anyway, what brings me in is that I keep starting my tasks, like the sanitation steps, the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork... and I just somehow always leave out the last parts. Even when I know my job completely depends on finishing them correctly. 

It's just... I get near the end of the forms, and, well, speaking of the end of the line, last week they actually moved me over to the poultry section. Have you ever been inside a poultry processing room? It is so incredibly loud. And my supervisor, Dave—he always wears these bright yellow rubber boots, which is so weird because literally everyone else wears white—he was yelling over the conveyor belts about something. Actually, seeing his boots reminded me that I really need to buy new ones for myself. My feet are always freezing because the floor is constantly covered in water from the washdown hoses, and mine have a leak in the left heel. 

Wait, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, I just keep leaving the last parts of my paperwork and sanitation steps unfinished, and I really can't afford to lose this job.

Do you ever feel like you have to double-check certain things, or do certain actions repeatedly, even if you know they might not make sense? Like a need to make sure something is done a certain way to prevent something bad from happening?

Um, no, not really. I don't think I do that. Like, I don't feel like I *have* to do things over and over to stop something bad from happening. Honestly, I'm usually just trying to get through the paperwork once, let alone twice. 

But speaking of doing things a certain way... my roommate, Sarah, she is so particular about the kitchen. She has this whole system for loading the dishwasher, and if I put a bowl in the wrong spot, she takes everything out and does it again. It drives me crazy. We actually got into an argument about it on Tuesday. Or was it Wednesday? No, Tuesday, because it was right after I watched that new documentary about deep-sea marine life. Have you seen it? The way those jellyfish glow in the dark is absolutely wild. It's called bioluminescence, I think. I spent like three hours looking up different types of glowing fish instead of doing my laundry. My laundry pile is huge right now, actually. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Something about double-checking things? Yeah, no, I don't really do that. I just... forget to finish them.
Have you noticed any changes in how well you can focus or concentrate on tasks lately, or if things that used to interest you don't seem to anymore?

Changes? Um... I don't think there's been a *change*, really. My focus has pretty much always been this bad. And I definitely haven't lost interest in things. If anything, I get interested in way too much stuff. 

Like, right now I'm completely obsessed with making my own hot sauce. We were talking about spicy food in the breakroom at the plant, and my coworker Miguel brought in these ghost peppers he grew himself. He has this entire hydroponic setup in his apartment, which is so cool. I actually went to the hardware store on Saturday to look at PVC pipes so I could build my own system, but I got totally distracted in the paint aisle. I spent like two hours just looking at all the different shades of green. I really want to paint my bedroom this nice sage color, but my roommate Sarah says our lease says we can't paint the walls. Which is so stupid because the current color is this awful beige that looks exactly like oatmeal. Do you like oatmeal? I can't stand the texture. It's just so mushy.

Wait, I'm doing it again, aren't I? Sorry. What was the question? Something about losing interest? Yeah, no, I still like my hobbies and stuff. I just can't seem to focus on the things I'm actually supposed to be doing.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or hopeless most days, or found little pleasure in doing things you usually enjoy?

Down or hopeless? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm stressed about work, obviously, because of the whole paperwork thing, but I don't feel depressed or anything. I still have a lot of fun doing things I like. 

Actually, yesterday I spent the whole afternoon trying to learn how to play the ukulele. I bought one at a garage sale over the weekend. It was only five dollars! The guy selling it was moving to Hawaii, which is so funny because that's where ukuleles are from, right? He said he was going to work on a macadamia nut farm. I love macadamia nuts, especially in those white chocolate cookies, though they're so expensive at the grocery store. I wonder why they cost so much more than peanuts. Peanuts grow underground, but macadamia nuts grow on trees. My grandma used to have a huge pecan tree in her backyard, and we'd spend hours picking them up in the fall. My hands would get so stained from the husks. 

Um, anyway, sorry. What were we talking about? Feeling down? Yeah, no, I feel fine mood-wise. I just get frustrated with myself for not getting things done.
